# nilpotent group　`def.nilpotent-group`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.nilpotent-group)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.nilpotent-group.md)

If there exists $c \ge 0$ with $\gamma_c = \{e\}$, then $G$ is **nilpotent**; the smallest such $c$ is the **nilpotency class** of $G$.

Equivalently, the **upper central series** $Z_0 = \{e\}$, $Z_{i+1}/Z_i := Z(G/Z_i)$ reaches $G$ in finitely many steps.

## Notes · **stale**
⭐ Examples: an abelian group has nilpotency class $1$ ($\gamma_1 = \{e\}$); $D_8$ has class $2$; every finite $p$-group is nilpotent; $S_3$ is not ($\gamma_1 = A_3$, $\gamma_2 = A_3 \ne \{e\}$).
